_about: The spine manifest. Read by deploy/checks/check-orphans.mjs (Phase 0 T4); that file's header
documents the heuristics, their known blind spots, and the ORPHAN_GATE=block switch.
TWO LISTS, TWO JOBS:
structures — spine columns and types that are supposed to be load-bearing. The gate counts
production READERS for each.
Zero readers was reported through Phases 0-1 and FAILS THE BUILD from the
PHASE-1 exit (2026-07-28): blocking is now the DEFAULT, ORPHAN_GATE=warn
is the only escape. Phase 1/2 tasks APPEND their new spine
columns here in their own commits.
tables     — every table in the migration chain that carries an agent link AND a state column.
Declaring is mandatory and ALWAYS blocking, from day one: an undeclared one fails
the build. This is the machine check for the plan's own falsifier — 'work/tracker
unification producing a second system in practice' (DOJO-OVERHAUL-PLAN Part VI).
workShaped answers ONE question, the OR1 test: do these rows track a unit of work whose
completion someone is owed, keyed to an agent? A table whose migration text shows a terminal
state may NOT be declared workShaped:false — the checker refuses that. 'why' is required on
every entry; a declaration nobody explained is a rubber stamp.
waivers — {entry, reason, date} suppress a zero-reader report for ONE structure. They are
printed and counted on every run. More than 5 across Arc 1 is the pre-committed signal that the
RULE is wrong and the rule gets fixed. Waivers do NOT apply to the table rule: an undeclared
work-shaped table is fixed by declaring it, which costs one entry and one sentence.
Every reader count in the AS-BUILT notes was measured by this checker at HEAD 6895eda on
2026-07-27; `node deploy/checks/check-orphans.mjs --explain <id>` reproduces any of them.
ZERO-READER DISPOSITIONS (added at the PHASE-1 exit, 2026-07-28, when the reader rule
flipped to blocking). Twelve of nineteen declared structures had no production reader at
the flip and the waiver budget is five, so the twelve were separated by WHAT IS ACTUALLY
TRUE about each instead of being waived in a heap:
waivers                        — the reader is inside packages/*/src and the heuristic
cannot see it. The GATE is wrong. Budget 5.
zeroReader.external-reader     — the reader is real, enumerated, and outside the scan
scope (the kit repo, watchdog/). Carries the reader's
path AND the command that re-derives it.
zeroReader.owed                — no reader exists anywhere; a NAMED phase owes one.
Carries owner + reason + date and prints on every run.
A zero-reader entry with none of the three FAILS the build. That is the flip.

structures.why: The stored monotonic sequence that replaces the (created_at, _tag, rowid) ordering key the two-store world needed. PROMOTED at T10 (migration 133): `seq` IS the table's `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`, so it is the rowid rather than a column kept equal to it by the `messages_seq_ai` trigger, which is deleted. AUTOINCREMENT is load-bearing, not decoration: without it SQLite reuses the largest rowid after the top row is deleted, and four live delete paths would then place a NEW row at an OLD position in every `ORDER BY seq` tail and below the vault archive high-water. Readers arrived with T5 (ORDER BY seq replaced the composite key everywhere); a bare `SELECT rowid` now returns a column NAMED `seq`, which is why every reader projects `seq AS rowid` and a source walk in memory/__tests__/lane-readers.test.ts refuses a bare one. READERS CONFIRMED at the PHASE-1 exit (2026-07-28, 41fcabb): 11 production files.

structures.why: Epoch-ms send time, the first spine column on this table to use the Part III time representation. Distinct from created_at (row-write time) so a delayed or retried send stops being indistinguishable from a fresh one. IT IS READ, and the gate cannot see it: message-store.ts projects it through the SELECT_COLS fragment constant (:117) at four sites (:344, :379, :435, :445) into StoredMessage.sentAt (:124). The gate requires the table name and the column name in the SAME string literal, and an interpolated `${SELECT_COLS}` is replaced by a placeholder before matching — the documented false-positive class, in the form T10 met from the other side (WAITING_COLS). Waived rather than dispositioned, because a waiver is exactly the claim being made: there IS a reader.

zeroReader.reason: CORRECTED BY PHASE-2 T8a, 2026-07-29. The previous disposition claimed kind='external-reader' with dojo-test-kit/behavioral/runner.mjs as the reader. That claim is FALSE about the tree, and it was re-run rather than believed: `git -C ../dojo-test-kit grep -nP "created_by_kind"` returns 15 hits and `... | grep -cP "legacy_tasks|legacy_projects"` returns 0. Every cited line reads agents.created_by_kind - runner.mjs:61 (a predicate on agents.name), :563 (the one-time adoption), :581 and :605 (both sweep prongs), bot.mjs:241/:306/:310, and kit-schema-conformance.mjs:162, which prepares "SELECT created_by_kind FROM agents". The sweep then deletes tracker rows by JOINING on created_by/assigned_to IN <harness agent ids> (runner.mjs:608 for tasks, :613 for projects) - it never consults the tracker's own copy. So this column has NO reader in production, in the kit, or in any test, which is why T8a's migration 137 deliberately did NOT carry it onto `work` (the Fork-A ruling's criterion is readers). The debt is settled by REMOVAL, not by wiring: T10 drops legacy_tasks/legacy_projects and this column goes with them. Recorded as a dated debt with an owner rather than a comfortable sentence - a false external-reader claim is worse than a declared orphan, because it stops the gate from asking the question at all.

structures.why: WHY a turn ended: a 17-value CHECKed enum, counted off DOJO-REBUILD-MAP.md:650-653 (research 19 s1c says 18 and is wrong). Half of the old `outcome` column, which conflated 'why did it end' with 'has the person heard from us' and made the second fact something ~29 sites re-derived from nine other variables. Written by agent/v2/turn-record.ts finalizeTurn + markTurnDied.

zeroReader.reason: T6's C1 cluster deletes the PROSE classification of a closeout (CLOSEOUT_PHRASE / CLOSEOUT_WHOLE_RE and their consumer, PHASE-2.md PINNED s11). The structural fact that replaces it is exactly 'how did this turn end', which is this column — so the task that removes the prose reader is the task that owes the column reader. Stated as an assignment with its reasoning so it can be challenged rather than inherited (#14): if T6 concludes the honest reader belongs elsewhere, it moves the owner and says why.

structures.why: WHETHER a genuine user-facing reply was DELIVERED this turn. 0/1, NOT NULL, no default — the writer must say, because 'we forgot to record it' and 'nothing was delivered' are the two facts this platform kept confusing. The other half of the old `outcome` split. HAS a production reader from the day it landed: tracker/delivery-evidence.ts:58 selects the answering turn with `answered = 1`, replacing the old `outcome = 'answered'` string test.

The counted non-idempotent call count for the turn, persisted instead of inferred. DEBT PAID — PHASE-2 T3, 2026-07-28. T2 wrote it once, at finalizeTurn, from the in-memory counter; T3 made it DURABLE at the effect (agent/v2/turn-record.ts bumpEffectfulCalls, called beside the counter's own increment in agent/v2/loop.ts) because a process killed between the effect and the end of the turn never reaches finalize, which is exactly the case the number exists to decide. finalizeTurn now raises it with MAX() and can never lower it. READER: work/store.ts reconcileOrphanedClaims() joins turns on work.claimed_by_turn at boot and holds any claim whose dead turn recorded effectful calls, so a killed turn's side effect is never repeated (P6b). Both directions are proven in work/__tests__/ask-lifecycle.test.ts (crash test B, the mechanical half).

The per-thread hop count, on the row instead of in the transport's own constant. INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, so it is honest from creation rather than nullable-until-someone-remembers. PAID PHASE-2 T4 2026-07-28: read and written by work/store.ts (threadHopCount/bumpThreadHopCount), enforced by the transport's gate against THREAD_HOP_CAP, which is now the tree's only declared value for the concept. MEASURED CORRECTION TO D2, recorded here because the debt was written from it: D2 says both caps fire; `git grep -n a2aIntentValidator HEAD` returns the definition and its own test file and NOTHING else, so the classifier's A2A_HOP_LIMIT=5 has no production caller and never rejected anything. SWEEP A still owns picking one value, and it now knows only one of them was ever live.

live | migrated | rescued, the same three values messages.provenance carries. It says where a work row came from, so a Stable Bridge import stays distinguishable from live traffic forever instead of being guessed from timestamps. UNLIKE messages.provenance, both values exist here from the first boot: migration 135's own copy stamps every legacy task and project 'migrated', so there is something real to distinguish on every box, not only after a Bridge run.

zeroReader.reason: The reader that matters is the one that treats a migrated row differently from a live one — a migrated `done` row points at a legacy-closure delivery (outcome='migrated'), not at a real send, and any surface that reports delivery history must be able to say so. T12 owns Bridge Entry 12 and is where that distinction becomes load-bearing. Recorded rather than closed early: a reader written now would have nothing to protect anyone from.

tables.name: work
tables.why: THE spine (OR1, PHASE-2 T2). One table, one ID space: `tasks` and `projects` became two `kind`s of one row with their ids carried over, and `done` is unreachable without a delivery to point at (CHECK state <> 'done' OR result_delivery_id IS NOT NULL). This is the table the falsifier is about, so it is declared first: if a SECOND work-shaped table ever appears beside it without an explanation in this file, the build stops, which is the whole point of the rule. NOTE for anyone extending the detector: `agent_id` deliberately carries NO foreign key and NO cascade (T0 D1) — a terminated agent's work rows must outlive their agent — so the absence of an FK here is a decision, not an oversight.
tables.disposition: LIVE, and the destination for everything else in this list. T3-T9 route their writers through work/store.ts's transition(); T10 drops the legacy tables it replaced.

tables.name: legacy_tasks
tables.why: THE tracker, now under its retirement name. PHASE-2 T2 copied every row into `work` with ids preserved and renamed the table in the same migration (135), so a reader nobody re-pointed fails loud instead of quietly reading a stale twin. It is still work-shaped and still declared, because it still holds rows and still has writers — 47 state-writing sites across 9 files, which the single-writer walk in work/__tests__ carries as a burn-down list. Note for anyone extending the detector: it links agents through `assigned_to TEXT REFERENCES agents(id)`, NOT a column named agent_id.
tables.disposition: Phase 2 — SUPERSEDED by `work` (OR1); renamed at T2, writers move at T8, table DROPS at T10.

tables.name: task_runs
tables.why: One row per execution of a task; part of the tasks family the plan names as partial work-tracking system #1. (It has never held a row in the live DB, and that is NOT evidence of deadness — rows are deleted with their tasks, and it has a live route, live UI and a conformance test: roadmap non-negotiable #15.)

tables.name: generation_jobs
tables.why: Per-agent async media-generation queue: queued -> running -> succeeded | failed (services/generation-jobs.ts). Structurally a work tracker keyed to an agent, and NOT one of the five the plan enumerated — recorded here so Phase 2 decides deliberately instead of discovering it later.
tables.disposition: TYPED SIDE-QUEUE — decided PHASE-2 T0, 2026-07-28. Not folded into work: its state is provider-side (provider_job_id, polling cadence, asset_path, cost_usd) and a finished asset nobody was shown is legitimately finished, which work.done's delivery requirement cannot express without sentinel deliveries. It already carries task_id + conversation_id, so the obligation is a work row and the job references it. The two-queues-one-lifecycle duplication with video_jobs is real and is SWEEP-F's.

tables.name: video_jobs
tables.why: The same shape again for video: queued -> polling -> succeeded | failed | cancelled (services/video-job-poller.ts). Two independent job queues with the same lifecycle is the duplication pattern this project exists to stop.
tables.disposition: TYPED SIDE-QUEUE — decided PHASE-2 T0, 2026-07-28. Same reasoning as generation_jobs; consolidation of the two queues is SWEEP-F's.

tables.name: healer_proposals
tables.why: Proposed fixes awaiting the owner's decision: pending -> approved | denied, with resolved_at (gateway/routes/healer.ts). A queue of things someone is owed a decision on, keyed to an agent.
tables.disposition: Sweep F owns the healer; the approval-routing pattern is explicitly promoted, not deleted.

tables.name: destructive_approvals
tables.why: A non-primary agent's held destructive tool call, waiting on the primary's decision (agent/destructive-gate.ts). Short-lived, but it is a per-agent row with a terminal state that someone is owed an answer on — declared true rather than argued down.
tables.disposition: Phase 5 rebuilds permissions; the approval flow (exact command, once) is on the preserve list.

tables.name: agents
tables.why: The agent registry itself. `status` is a PROCESS lifecycle (idle | working | paused | error | terminated), not a unit of work, and the agent link the detector found is the self-referential spawn edge `parent_agent`. Caught by the structural trigger and declared not-work on purpose — the detector is deliberately over-eager.

tables.name: turns
tables.why: The turn record. `outcome` (answered | no_reply | parked | handoff | aborted | brake | error) says how a TURN ended, not whether an obligation is outstanding. A spine table in its own right (Part III).
tables.disposition: Stays and grows — turn identity allocated at turn start in Phase 2.

tables.name: deliveries
tables.why: The delivery ledger: one row per send attempt, `outcome` (delivered | failed | held) recording how the send went. It is the EVIDENCE a piece of work finished, not a second place where work is tracked.
tables.disposition: Stays and becomes universal in Phase 2 (recorded at the five transport doors).

tables.name: techniques
tables.why: An authored artifact, not a job. `state` is an editorial lifecycle (draft | review | published) on a document that has no completion anyone is owed.
tables.disposition: Sweep D — equip/export/import integrity; the table stays.

tables.name: twilio_call_log
tables.why: A transport log mirroring Twilio's own call status for a phone call that already happened. No work is claimed, assigned or completed here.
tables.disposition: Sweep B — voice/phone consolidation; the log stays.

waivers.reason: FALSE POSITIVE, measured: the column IS read. memory/message-store.ts builds its projection from the SELECT_COLS fragment constant (:116-118) and interpolates it into four `SELECT ${SELECT_COLS} FROM messages` statements (:344, :379, :435, :445), landing in StoredMessage.sentAt (:124). The heuristic requires table and column inside ONE string literal and blanks `${...}` before matching, so a shared column list is invisible to it — the documented false-positive class (the same shape T10 hit from the other side with counterparty.ts's WAITING_COLS). RIDER, stated because it is the weaker half of the truth: the SQL reads it, but nothing downstream CONSUMES StoredMessage.sentAt yet. This gate asks about SQL readers; the consumption question is Sweep E's with the rest of the wire shape.
